title: bug: an architect's exit checkpoint lands the live assignee's in-flight bytes for the task it planned, so the worker's completion is NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and the DONE task has no completion commit
description:
Observed 2026-10-25 by governor-187cc44e on CQ-I01 task-96526848b23549cf994ab82f47fad29f.

Timeline:
- Codex architect-473624b4's session (pre-flight 09:51:54Z) claimed I01 at pre-flight. It planned I01 at 09:58:13; TURBO auto-approved it to WORKING.
- worker-9cda703c claimed I01 at 09:58:22 and worked steps 1-6. Step 6 started at 10:09:43 and completed at 10:14:37.
- At 10:13:23 the architect session exited. Its wrapper landed checkpoint 263e9f5, `wip(task-96526848…) [status=WORKING role=architect]`, which held the worker's in-flight source bytes: docs/MCP_SERVER.md, server/WebSocketServer.ts, server/WebSocketServer.test.ts and server/clientCapabilities.ts (+412/-12).
- The worker's completion at 10:17:12 returned MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.
- qa_approve at 10:59:26 raised ⚠️ NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT. task.landing is null on a DONE task whose bytes ARE on the branch. A governor has to reconstruct this by hand every time.

Same shape: 1f9c7d5 (architect-6e3edf85's exit checkpoint on WORKING task-5f3960df).

Cause: the wrapper lands its session's pre-flight task at exit even after that task moved to another live assignee. getCommitScope.ts says there is no ownership guard; orphan mode exists for crash recovery. Interactive architects exit often through the account-switch mod, so this keeps happening.

Effects:
- Mid-edit worker bytes get committed and pushed as a wip under the wrong role, which can break the branch at that commit.
- The completion commit goes missing, along with landing metadata and the Moe-Contested trailer evidence.
- False NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT alarms.

Expected: a session that is not the task's assignee, while the assignee is live or holds an open attempt, lands no source path for that task. It may still land the task's own board record. The bytes stay dirty for the assignee's own landing. Orphan recovery is unchanged when the assignee is dead or absent.

Files: scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (twins), scripts/tests/postflight.sh and .ps1, and possibly packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts (expose the assignee's liveness). The wrapper and postflight files are currently contested by the stale task-07474ee438f34021a23809f9c764d15c. Plan for a Claude Edit/Write seat, or wait for that contest to clear. Serialize behind task-c532d223459b4ef4b5bab2ba0eb4005e and task-5c71dff9ff2a488d8f75ec375c4f99f8, which edit moe-agent.sh.
definitionOfDone: A non-assignee session exit (architect/QA/governor) on a task whose assignee is a live worker, or holds an open execution attempt, lands no source path for that task. The skip is reported with a named code and through record_commit. The assignee's own later completion commits those bytes, so the task gets a completion commit and landing metadata.
Orphan recovery is unchanged: when the assignee is dead or absent, or the task is unassigned, the existing checkpoint landing still happens. The sh and ps1 wrappers behave identically.

The postflight harness has a case for each behavior in both postflight.sh and postflight.ps1, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes. If the daemon is touched, cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test exits 0.
scripts/CLAUDE.md 'Land on every exit' documents the live-assignee rule.

implementationPlan.description: Read landed prerequisites, producer assigneeProtected contract, original DoD and baseline ownership memories. Map every path that can collect live working-tree bytes: run_landing/Invoke-MoeLanding, recovery re-entry, teardown_rescue/Invoke-MoeRescueRef, and any precomputed scope passed into them. Do not edit daemon/shared fake proxy in this task. Confirm source-changing paths all funnel through the guard while receipt replay of an already-landed immutable commit remains unchanged.
implementationPlan.note:
Mapped every working-tree source entrance.

sh:
- run_landing. Post-flight passes LAND_SCOPE_FILE=''. The pre-flight recovery in preflight_landing reuses the pre-flight scope.json via LAND_SCOPE_FILE; it will be refreshed. The daemon's phase is echo-only.
- teardown_rescue. It runs its own commit_scope postflight, then resolve_attribution, then rescue_ref teardown. FROZEN_TREE is built only inside run_landing, after the guard point.
- The gate, peel, commit and ref-contention rescues all run after attribution inside run_landing.

ps1:
- Invoke-MoeLanding, for post-flight and for recovered landings via Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck and Invoke-MoeIdleRecovery.
- Invoke-MoeTeardownRescue calls Invoke-MoeRescueRef 'teardown'. Its own scope is used when Attr is null; there is also a frozen-tree branch.

Plan for the guard:
- One ownership-verdict function per wrapper, placed right after the scope fetch in each landing and teardown entrance, before baseline_landed_flag/BL copy, attribution, peel, private index and rescue.
- On a refusal: no baseline write, no landed mark, no attempt close (finalize is worker-only and pinned to its own attempt), and MOE_LANDING_DONE/moeLandingDone set.
- Receipt replay (receipt_replay / Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay) re-reports already-landed immutable commits and stays untouched.

Finalizing-window decision (QA comment on producer task-9a9b46d8): the guard will also refuse with MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE when the task is unassigned or held by an unprotected foreign owner AND .moe/attempts holds a well-formed foreign attempt in phase 'finalizing' for the task. This mirrors the daemon's finalizing hold (util/claimEligibility.ts isHoldingFinalizingAttempt / foreignFinalizingAttempt, which already bars every other seat from claiming that row). DoD #2 still holds: a genuinely orphaned unassigned task, or a dead owner with a closed attempt, still lands.

The fake proxy has no scope-failure knob, and editing it is out of scope. The disk-fallback scenario will use the fake's documented invalid-knob exit-1 path.

No files modified.

implementationPlan.description: Use test-driven-development to add compact equivalent postflight scenarios in both harnesses, using the producer's shared fake-proxy controls. Matrix: own assignee allowed; foreign architect/QA/governor vs protected owner refused (include protection true with presence false to represent quiet/open-attempt owner); dead/missing owner with protection false and explicitly unassigned task still checkpoint; foreign owner with omitted/malformed protection refuses. Protected exit must log/record named refusal, create no source commit/rescue/push, leave source hash/dirty status and baseline header/content unchanged, and preserve shared index. In a sequential same-repo scenario, first foreign exit refuses, then rightful worker completion includes the source bytes and reports committed completion/ref/paths instead of nothing; verify ledger completion shape consumed by landing metadata. Cover daemon-failure/disk fallback and teardown after refusal so a signal cannot recover protected bytes. Keep existing orphan/recovery scenarios intact and update counts only for genuinely added cases.
implementationPlan.note: Scope growth: new shared suite scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs (same reason as the shared fake proxy: one case list runs on both engines, so sh and ps1 cannot drift). postflight.sh/.ps1 call it after the frozen suite. Cases (12, self-counted): own, active (architect vs live worker), quiet (qa vs alive=0 protected=1), omitted / malformed protection, fallback-owner (RPC down + foreign owner on disk), finalizing (unassigned + foreign finalizing attempt), recovered (pre-flight recovery vs live owner), dead, unassigned, fallback-unassigned, sequential (architect refuses, then the owner's completion commits the bytes: committed completion row with sha/ref/paths, no NOTHING_TO_COMMIT). A refusal must leave refs/HEAD/index/porcelain/owned-file hash/baseline unchanged, push nothing, record refused rows with code/role/session, and print commit=none outcome=refused code=<code>. Frozen suite: new teardown-protected mode (Ctrl+C on a task another worker owns: no rescue/candidate/gate, one refused rescue row with ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE, baseline unchanged). Existing scenarios and counts untouched. RED: sh and ps1 (powershell 5.1) give the same result: own/dead/unassigned/fallback-unassigned pass, the other 8 fail 'a refused exit leaves refs, tree, index and baseline as they were'. Frozen teardown-protected fails 'nothing is parked, frozen or gated' on sh and ps1 (current code writes a rescue ref).

implementationPlan.description: Implement equivalent fail-closed ownership decisions in both wrapper scope readers/landing paths. Validate task identity and assignedWorkerId; own caller may land, explicit unassigned may land, a different owner may land only when authoritative assigneeProtected is boolean false. Different owner with true refuses using MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE; missing/malformed/unreadable protection or ownership refuses with MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_OWNER_UNKNOWN. Error handling: RPC failure or old daemon lacking the field must not be coerced into false; disk fallback may only allow a positively identified own/unassigned task, never infer a foreign owner dead. Refresh cached preflight scope before source landing. Place guard before attribution, baseline pruning/landed marking, branch peel, private-index build and source rescue; ensure teardown/recovery cannot bypass it, including signal cleanup and prebuilt working-tree candidates. Refuse the whole landing (board-only is optional and intentionally omitted), send record_commit outcome refused with task/session/role/code, set existing summary/handled flags so cleanup does not retry; report ledger failure best-effort without mutating Git or losing bytes. Keep owned immutable receipt replay/finalization behavior and orphan checkpoint logic unchanged.
implementationPlan.note:
Owner guard in both wrappers. sh: landing_owner_guard + landing_refuse_owner. ps1: Get-MoeOwnerGuard (fetches the scope; any exception -> OWNER_UNKNOWN) + Send-MoeOwnerRefusal.
Rule:
- The owner (== own workerId) lands.
- A foreign owner refuses: ACTIVE on assigneeProtected===true; OWNER_UNKNOWN when not a JSON bool, on the disk fallback, or with a missing/malformed owner or taskId mismatch.
- Unassigned, or a foreign owner with an explicit false, scans .moe/attempts for a well-formed foreign `finalizing` attempt on the task (ACTIVE) and otherwise lands (orphan path unchanged).
- The disk fallback emits assignedWorkerId only when the record has the key. All 477 records and taskStore create always write it.
Placement:
- run_landing / Invoke-MoeLanding: before the baseline read, snapshot, attribution, gate, peel, temp index and rescue.
- Pre-flight recovery: refreshes the scope (sh LAND_SCOPE_FILE=''; ps1 already fresh).
- Teardown: guard before the [rescue] line and the frozen-tree branch. ps1 passes the guard's scope to Invoke-MoeRescueRef via a new -Scope param, so the rescue makes no second fetch.
Refusal behaviour:
- record_commit outcome refused with code/role/sessionId and no sha/ref/push/path fields.
- Session-ended line reads commit=none ... outcome=refused code=...
- Landing-done is set, so there is no teardown double pass.
Checks:
- bash -n OK; ParseFile OK on PS 5.1 + pwsh 7; BOM kept; parity-check.sh PASS.
- Owner-guard suite 12/12 on sh, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7.
- Frozen teardown-{protected,running,finalizing,scope,recovered} 5/5 on sh and PS 5.1.
Step-2 test fix: the sequential case now normalizes the ledger `ref`. ps1 records refs/heads/<branch> where sh records <branch>; that is a pre-existing wrapper difference, filed as task-3d0be5681276428d8908d361341145bf (bug, LOW).
The shared checkout has ~608 foreign dirty paths; none were touched.

implementationPlan.note:
scripts/CLAUDE.md "Land on every exit" gains an **Owner guard** paragraph:
- Where it runs: post-flight landing, pre-flight recovery on a fresh scope, and teardown rescue.
- Non-assignee sessions land no source or BOARD bytes while assigneeProtected is true, or while another seat's attempt is finalizing: MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review done; no defects, NO byte changes in this step (owned paths clean, identical to checkpoint 37ed6ae; diff vs bb35a16^ = +427/-29, net 398). Covered: assignment changing after preflight (guard re-reads get_commit_scope at landing/teardown time; preflight recovery uses a fresh scope); protected owner that is quiet or has no worker record but an open attempt (assigneeProtected -> ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE); a foreign closed attempt (only a well-formed foreign `finalizing` attempt blocks, so a closed one lands); malformed/null/string booleans, missing/malformed owner, taskId mismatch, disk fallback (all except JSON false -> OWNER_UNKNOWN); RPC/python/PS exceptions (fail closed -> OWNER_UNKNOWN); concurrent source edits, baseline owned by another session, shared index (refusal runs before any baseline/snapshot/temp-index/ref work and touches none of them); signals (refusal sets MOE_LANDING_DONE / $moeLandingDone, so the trap/finally does not re-land). Every working-tree landing entrance runs the same predicate: post-flight landing, pre-flight recovery, teardown rescue (sh+ps1). No refusal marks a baseline landed, closes an attempt, or records a phantom row: record_commit outcome=refused has no sha/ref/push/paths. Own completion, plus orphan recovery for a dead or absent owner or an unassigned task, still land (owner-guard cases own/dead/unassigned/fallback-unassigned/recovered/sequential). Landed checkpoints a2441f5/bb35a16/309c1dd/37ed6ae carry only owned paths + board JSON. Known limits, no fix: (1) the scope read and the branch CAS are two steps, not an atomic daemon/Git check (documented in scripts/CLAUDE.md); (2) a catchable throw inside ps1 Send-MoeOwnerRefusal would reach the finally rescue (practically unreachable); (3) the finalizing scan reads all .moe/attempts (~1.3 s for 551 files on /mnt/d), only when the owner is null or unprotected; (4) the OWNER_UNKNOWN WARN says 'not its owner'; (5) teardown refused rows differ in status/cliExit between sh and ps1, as their old rescue rows did; (6) a deleted task record refuses and leaves the bytes dirty; (7) a stale finalizing attempt blocks non-owner landing until finalize_attempt; (8) a daemon without assigneeProtected refuses foreign-owner landing, by design. Filed bug task-3d0be568 (sh vs ps1 ledger ref form). Identical final gate re-running fresh on HEAD 7c7ce76 (owned+harness sha256 == run 1).

comments.author: architect-2c9d5121
comments.content:
Producer plan for task-9a9b46d88ff244759570c323ac3a67a4 was submitted 2026-10-27 and is in WORKING. Build your scenarios against these names.
(1) get_commit_scope.assigneeProtected (boolean):
- false: task unassigned (null, undefined or '').
- true: the owner's worker record exists and is not DEAD. lastActivityAt is never consulted.
- true: an attempt for this task has workerId === owner and phase !== 'closed'. An unknown phase also counts.
- Fail-closed true: a non-string assignedWorkerId, or a worker record with no status.
- The value is the same whoever calls. assigneeAlive is unchanged (presence only).
(2) Fake-proxy knobs, changed from the description:
- FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE: unset or EMPTY means the caller is the assignee (today's behaviour). The sentinel 'none' means unassigned. Any other value is that worker id. Empty cannot mean unassigned because PowerShell deletes an env var set to '', so postflight.ps1 could never express it.
- FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE_ALIVE=0|1 is added so you can model a protected-but-quiet owner (alive 0, protected 1).
- FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE_PROTECTED=0|1.
- FAKE_SCOPE_OWNERSHIP_MODE=omit|malformed. 'malformed' returns the boolean as a string, so 'false' arrives as a string that must not be coerced.
- A caller that is not the assignee is added to activePeerIds and makes peersActive true, as in the daemon's orphan rule.
- An invalid knob value makes the fake exit 1.

comments.author: qa-6fa5d758
comments.content:
QA note from producer task-9a9b46d8 (approved). It names one window the producer field does not cover, for your step-3 rule and step-6 review.
- complete_task clears assignedWorkerId on WORKING→REVIEW, but the completing worker's attempt stays open in `finalizing` until its wrapper lands and calls finalize_attempt (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeTask.ts, comment at ~L209).
- In that window get_commit_scope answers assignedWorkerId null and assigneeProtected false. That is deliberate per the producer spec: unassigned is false even with a former worker's open attempt, and a test pins it.
- So your "explicit unassigned may land" lets a foreign session that exits in those seconds land the worker's completion bytes as its own checkpoint. An example is the planning architect, whose pre-flight task this is. The worker's completion would then be NOTHING_TO_COMMIT: the parent bug's shape in a narrower window.
- A QA claim cannot interleave there: the claim path refuses a row that holds a foreign `finalizing` attempt (claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt / util/claimEligibility.ts).
- To close the window you need a signal beyond assigneeProtected. One option is a foreign open attempt on an unassigned REVIEW task, read from .moe/attempts/; another is a follow-up producer field. Weigh that against your DoD #2, under which unassigned keeps orphan landing.

Rule (sh landing_owner_guard, ps1 Get-MoeOwnerGuard; **Owner guard** in scripts/CLAUDE.md):
- The assignee lands.
- Foreign owner with assigneeProtected true, or another seat's well-formed `finalizing` attempt (QA's window note): MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE.
- Foreign owner with an absent/non-boolean answer, malformed owner, taskId mismatch, failed check or disk fallback: MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_OWNER_UNKNOWN.
- Unassigned, or foreign owner with JSON false and nothing finalizing: lands as before (orphan recovery unchanged).
Runs first in post-flight landing, pre-flight recovery (fresh scope) and teardown rescue. A refusal touches no tree, index, ref or baseline; it records record_commit outcome=refused (code, role, sessionId, no paths), prints commit=none outcome=refused code=..., and sets landing-done so teardown cannot re-land.
